content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For less urgent cases, contact a poison control center. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. Additionally, laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney and liver function assessments, should be conducted while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. Possible side effects of this medication include skin tingling, chills, goosebumps, stomach pain, or urinary issues such as frequent or difficult urination. Less common side effects may include dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, trouble sleeping, or leg cramps. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Rarely, this drug may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using this medication, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. For any questions or concerns about this medication, always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice.
